extracted.intended_audience: Citizens and ratifiers evaluating the proposed federal Constitution (readers of The Federalist / informed public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing whether a proposed constitution conforms to republican principles and adequately balances stability, energy, and liberty; includes standards for judging the work of a constitutional convention and responses to common objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of critics
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics should not approach the proposed Constitution with a predisposition to censure or a predetermination to condemn; papers are addressed only to those with sincere zeal for the country's happiness and a temper favorable to a just estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of authors who 'scanned the proposed Constitution...with a predetermination to condemn' or who display opposite bias. Give weight only to opinions formed without predetermined hostility or partisanship; seek critics who aim at a fair discussion and accurate judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for fallibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the plan bearing in mind that a faultless plan was not to be expected and the convention, being composed of fallible men, could err.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume infallibility in rejudging the fallible opinions of others; allow for human error in framing and judging constitutional provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of novelty and lack of useful precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: The undertaking is novel; other confederacies are vitiated by erroneous principles and can only serve as warning beacons, not templates to be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect difficulties arising from novelty; prefer a design that avoids known past errors and provides means to correct future mistakes as experience unfolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of stability and energy with republican liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: A constitution must combine requisite stability and energy in government with inviolable attention to liberty and republican form; this mingling is difficult and requires due proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the plan secures security, prompt execution of laws, and national character (stability/energy) while preserving powers derived from the people, short terms, and diffusion of offices (liberty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy in government
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy in government is essential to security against external/internal danger and to prompt and salutary execution of the laws; it generally requires a certain duration of power and execution by a single hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the proposed structure provides effective, decisive means for conducting national defense and enforcing laws; evaluate tenure and concentration of executive authority as contributors to energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability in government
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability is essential to national character, the advantages annexed to it, and public repose and confidence; frequent changes produce irregular legislation and are odious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether tenure lengths and institutional continuity promote steady policy and public confidence without sacrificing republican accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republican tenure and diffusion of offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Republican genius seems to demand that power be derived from the people, that those entrusted with it be kept independent of the people by short durations, and that trust be placed in a number of hands rather than a few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate term lengths, modes of appointment, and the number of officeholders to ensure popular derivation and diffusion of power consistent with republicanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension between single-hand execution and multiple hands
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy requires unity (single hand) and duration; republican principles favor diffusion and short terms; the constitution must navigate this tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether the plan reasonably compromises between centralized execution (for energy) and distributed authority (for liberty), e.g., through checks, term structures, and separation of functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper partition of general and State authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Marking the line of partition between the authority of the general and State governments is difficult but essential; clear boundaries are needed despite inherent vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the Constitution delineates federal versus state powers with workable clarity and mechanisms to resolve inevitable borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept unavoidable ambiguity and provide correction mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Obscurity arises from indistinctness of objects, imperfection of human conception, and inadequacy of language; any definition will have some obscurity, especially for complex and novel objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a plan in light of unavoidable imprecision; prefer provisions that include practical mechanisms (adjudication, amendments) to liquidate and ascertain meanings over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for varied local interests and regional differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Different local positions, policies, districts, and classes produce contending interests and local jealousies that complicate framing a national government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether the plan accommodates diversity of interests among large/small states and regions, and whether it provides institutions that mediate competing local concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of compromise between large and small states
rubrics_metrics.description: Compromise between larger and smaller states in representation and structure was inevitable; theoretical propriety sometimes had to yield to extraneous considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether compromises (e.g., representation ratios) are reasonable given the need to secure union and whether they produce durable, acceptable arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of factional animosities
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention's success depended on an unusual exemption from party animosities, which commonly contaminate deliberative bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the plan's adoption process and institutions reduce factional capture and encourage sacrifice of private partial interests for the public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to sacrifice private interests for public good
rubrics_metrics.description: Deputation consent indicates that members were induced to sacrifice private opinions and partial interests to public good and despair of improvement by delay or new experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the plan's capacity to produce compromises where necessary public sacrifices are made; check for mechanisms that encourage collective resolution over factional insistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic standard: better, not perfect
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed constitution need not be perfect; it is sufficient that it is more perfect than the existing Confederation—compare reforms pragmatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the new plan to the status quo (Articles of Confederation); prioritize relative improvement and problem-solving over theoretical perfectionism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of objections and availability of alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectors often disagree among themselves and fail to present a coherent alternative remedy; if opponents cannot agree on a substitute, the proposed remedy recommended unanimously by the convention should be preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating objections, require coherent, mutually-consistent alternative proposals; weigh the absence of agreement among objectors against the convention's unanimous recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical-test/experiment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Some errors in a constitutional plan may only be ascertainable by actual trial; the plan should be judged with the expectation of future adjustments based on experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that certain defects will emerge only in practice; prefer plans that are workable and amendable rather than speculative perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for effective powers commensurate to objects
rubrics_metrics.description: A government must have regular powers adequate to its objects; otherwise it will either be impotent or will usurp and overreach in practice (dissolution or usurpation dilemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the Constitution grants authorities and resources (revenue, troop-raising, administration of territories) necessary to perform national functions without encouraging unconstitutional assumption of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison consistency: criticisms must apply to existing system too
rubrics_metrics.description: Many objections to the new plan (indefinite taxing power, troop raising, mixing powers, lack of bill of rights, treaties as law, slave importation term-limits) apply equally or worse to the existing Confederation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate objections by testing whether the same faults are present in the current system; require critics to account for relative differences rather than asserting absolute condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'republic' for conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: A republic is defined as a government deriving all powers directly or indirectly from the people, administered by persons holding office during pleasure, for a limited period, or during good behavior; essential that it be derived from the great body of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conformity by checking popular derivation of authority, appointment modes (direct/indirect), and tenures (limited periods or good behavior); ensure no minority or privileged class exclusively controls power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency test for republican character
rubrics_metrics.description: It is sufficient for a government to be republican that persons administering it be appointed directly or indirectly by the people and hold their appointments under the tenures specified (pleasure, limited period, good behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the practical test: if leadership is chosen by the people (directly/indirectly) and tenures are of the republican sorts, the government conforms to the republican standard even if some offices are indirectly appointed.
